origin.description: Returns localizable month, weekday, quarter, AM/PM, and era names.

arguments.name: locale
arguments.text: NULL or "" for the default locale. @calendar=name selects that calendar's names.

arguments.name: context
arguments.text: format or standalone. A unique prefix is enough.

arguments.name: width
arguments.text: abbreviated, wide, or narrow. A unique prefix is enough.

origin.details: Month, Weekday, Quarter, AmPm, and Era. Weekday starts at Sunday. A locale with no calendar keyword uses the locale's date-format symbols, which can differ from that locale's default calendar.
origin.value: A named list of character vectors.

translation.description: Month, weekday, quarter, AM/PM, and era names for a locale.

arguments.name: locale
arguments.text: None or "" for the default locale. @calendar=name selects that calendar's names.

arguments.name: context
arguments.text: format or standalone. A unique prefix is enough.

arguments.name: width
arguments.text: abbreviated, wide, or narrow. A unique prefix is enough.

translation.details: A calendar keyword is passed to ICU's date-format symbols. With no keyword, the locale's symbols are used as they stand. Narrow eras and quarters are read from ICU because those two calls are not wrapped by PyICU.
translation.value: A dict with keys Month, Weekday, Quarter, AmPm, and Era. Each value is a list of strings.
translation.example:
from stringi.datetime import stri_datetime_symbols
x = stri_datetime_symbols("en_US")["Month"][0]
print(f'stri_datetime_symbols("en_US")$Month[1] is {x}.')
